A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the revised proofs and new Appendix E in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original Monte-Carlo simulations and LLM self-improvement experiments on synthetic shortest-path tasks, GSM8K, and DeepMind Mathematics.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation and model-training results reported in Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 5.1 retain the same generation, reward filtering, maximum-likelihood update, and easy-to-hard curriculum procedures. Appendix E discusses possible extensions without implementing a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic shortest-path task, GSM8K, and DeepMind Mathematics modules and difficulty levels. The noisy-reward and test-time settings discussed in v3 are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The fixed uniform-mixture comparator and the evaluated Llama and Qwen model roster remain unchanged. The newly cited test-time methods do not participate in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain the same Pass@1 evaluation, data splits, model sizes, question and answer budgets, iteration counts, and curriculum mixing settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the same analyses of initialization, task difficulty, question budgets, per-question answer budgets, and adjacent difficulty separation, including collapse and saturation observations. No new empirical robustness or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 retains five-run averaging with different seeds for Figures 3–4. Figure 4(b)'s aggregation across 15 initializations and standard-error shading, and Table 4's standard-error reporting, are unchanged.

E6.justification: The empirical tables and plotted simulation/experimental results are unchanged. For example, both report Qwen3-8B's GSM8K trajectory as 27.52, 28.66, 29.75, and 30.67 in Table 1; Table 4 also retains all scores and standard errors.

T1.justification: Corollary 5.6, formalized as Corollary C.4 in v3, replaces the global unique-optimizer guarantee with a guarantee on qualified finite intervals [0,B], with B-dependent smallness conditions. It changes the large-difficulty threshold scaling from Θ(2^(-β'/2)) to O(2^(-β')). Appendix C.4 substantially revises the supporting arguments and adds strict-convexity and moment-inequality proofs in Lemmas C.10–C.11.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same principal claims about finite-sample self-improvement, acceptance feedback, conditions favoring easy-to-hard curricula, and empirical validation. The revised corollary does not rewrite those overarching claims.

C2.justification: Remark 5.7.3 qualifies the optimal-difficulty interpretation to finite intervals. New Appendix E explains the clean-verification limitation, requirements for extending the analysis to noisy rewards, and why the current bounds do not directly apply to other test-time training objectives or update rules.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the prompt templates, graph-generation procedure, CP-SAT data selection, training instructions, and settings in Tables 6–8. No new implementation or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix E adds positioning relative to test-time computation through citations to SETS, Learning to (Learn at Test Time), and Test-Time Training Done Right. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: v3 presents Corollary 5.6 informally and places its formal statement in Appendix C.4, adds Appendix E, and clarifies the auxiliary infinite-limit argument. It also adds an ICML acceptance note and updates bibliographic text; the overall narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: All five figures and eight tables are retained. Figures 4–5 and Tables 1 and 3 move earlier, with accompanying text and table reflow; the graphical content and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves an important inconsistency: v2's Lemma C.7 derives an O(2^(-β')) upper bound but concludes Θ(2^(-β'/2)). The revision retains the compatible bound, confines the optimizer guarantee to controlled finite intervals, and adds convexity and moment arguments. These changes substantially improve the mathematical support for a central curriculum conclusion, despite narrowing its scope. The empirical evidence is preserved, and Appendix E clarifies applicability.
